page.layout: Running head at top, with page number at top left. Two engraved medallions with rim legends side by side, centred above the text. Below them one block of running text in two paragraphs, full width. No margin notes, no catchword or signature.

main_text.p: CLEMENS, huius nóminis Papa feptimus, Adriano fupradicto in Pontificatu succeffit anno mundi 5484. à Christo nato 1522. Hic antea Iulius vocabatur, sed Cardinalium quorundam fuafu, Clementis nomen assumpsit. Fuit Leo decimus huic patruelis. Dicitur Clemens fauisse Francorum Regi Francisco etiam capto, aduerfus Cæsarem Carolu: ideoq; Romā ab exercitu Cæsaris, cui præerat Carolus Borbonius, direptā ac expilatam, nihilominus tamen ab hoc coronā accepit Carolus imperialem, præterea sacram vnctionem: fuit rarissimi ac callidissimi ingenij. Frācisci Valesij partes iterum secutus, ad Massiliam cum eo conuenit, initúmque est marrimoniū[?] proneptis fuæ Catharinæ Laurentij Medices Ducis Vrbinatis filiæ, cum Henrico Duce Aurelianensi, nunc autem Francorum Rege. Florētiam vrbem patriam obsedit, quā post annum obsidionis cepit: Ducémque in ea constituit Alexādrū Medices, prædicti Laurentij Medices filium naturalem. Aiunt prouocatum à Florentinis id bellum gessisse, qui in cognatos ac necessarios huius Clementis infesti essent, atque etiā in ipsum Pontificem infensi: vitio tamen illi interim vertitur, quôd in patriam ita fæuierit, quam etiam velut sub iugum miserit: fedit annis 12. Vide Iouium, Supplem. Chro. & Platinam.

ODETVS de Foix, dictus Lautretius, Mediolani sub Francisco Valesio praefectus, deinde exercitus Gallici in Italia Dux, Papiā & Alexandriā expugnauit: Neapolim exercitu duxit: quô dū tederet Clementi, quē Aurafiensis Princeps sub custodia tenebat, opē attulit: Porrò vbi Neapolim peruenit, arridētis fortunæ occasione captare nesciuit: nā cominus si vrbē aggressus esset, hāc facilè cepisset: sed interim dū eminus nimis cūctatur, Neapolis auxiliares Hispanos milites recipit: tandē tum ob aeris intemperantiam, tum ob aquas veneno infectas cum multis aliis Gallorū primoribus periit an. D. 1528. Vide Suppl. & Iouium.

page.notes: Two engraved medallions above the text, with rim legends transcribed above; the legend at the lower left of the right medallion is partly cut off, so "S DE LAL" is doubtful. Doubtful readings: "marrimoniū" (type broken at the word, likely matrimonium). The text is set in roman type with macrons and some ligatures (ff, ss), all rendered with plain s. No marginal notes.
